verdicts.message: Medium: gcm-no-tag-length: The call to 'createDecipheriv' with the Galois Counter Mode (GCM) mode of operation is missing an expected authentication tag length. If the expected authentication tag length is not specified or otherwise checked, the application might be tricked into verifying a shorter-than-expected authentication tag. This can be abused by an attacker to spoof ciphertexts or recover the implicit authentication key of GCM, allowing arbitrary forgeries.
verdicts.reason: createDecipheriv in GCM mode without authTagLength accepts a truncated authentication tag (Node accepts 4-byte tags), weakening the integrity the field cipher promises. Accidental, not a plant.
verdicts.action: repo fixed in a1e3218: authTagLength 16 on cipher and decipher; a test proves a 4-byte tag is refused

verdicts.message: Changelog looks stale/thin: The changelog this check read carries 2 versioned entries, against a bar of 3. Counted as either an `x.y.z` string or a version-shaped section heading (`## [1.2.0]`, `## V14.x.x`, `## Updates in 8.0.x`), whichever is the larger — so a log sectioned by minor series counts its sections, not its individual patch numbers. Entries recorded somewhere this check does not read — release notes generated at tag time from a generator config it did not recognise, or a log kept outside the repository — are not counted here, and this row is about what is re-findable in the tree rather than about how often you release.

verdicts.message: Interpolated log message defeats structured logging: `warn` at line 51 is handed a template literal with `${…}` substitutions as its message, so the logger receives one finished string — the values in it cannot be queried, filtered or aggregated as fields, and every occurrence reads as a different message. Pass the values beside a constant message instead: `logger.warn({ orderId, status }, 'order status updated')` for pino and bunyan, `logger.warn('order status updated', { orderId, status })` for winston. If these calls go through a NestJS `Logger` routed into pino, nestjs-pino forwards an object first argument as fields in the same way.
verdicts.reason: The e-mail gateway's warning interpolated the HTTP status into the message.
verdicts.action: repo fixed in a1e3218: status passed as a field, constant message

Five of the seven FNs are population gaps of the TypeScript arm by construction: DM9, DM10 and DM11 have no TypeScript arm, DM7 cannot read a TypeScript repository's subject type, and DM6 on TypeScript reads ORM decorators only (a domain service querying knex is invisible). One is unmapped (consent-not-checked). One (BTL-001) was found by D23 but is location-less.

The host --with-llm passes on this box have no TypeScript code model (the sidecar's node modules are not installed beside the host engine): every DM/AX7/D23 card disappears and recall drops to 0/11. Model-judged rows (M4 100, D19 90, D21 100) raised nothing; the default and gdpr-tech host passes are byte-identical. LA1 could not be measured in either configuration.
